candidates.title: Identical runs asked at once keep one row whose by and created_by name different askers
candidates.statement: When the same run request arrives more than once at the same moment, every ask computes, every ask is told the run is its own, and the one row keeps the first insert's created_by beside the last writer's body by and at.
candidates.contract: docs/api/engines.md:541-544: "The same request twice is one row, answered as it was first kept: its `by` and `created_by` are the first asker's, whoever asks again. `created_by` is the `runs` table's column for the asker ... served on every run as `EngineRun.by`, and check 8 reads both"
candidates.reproCommand: bughunt/notes/H1/scripts/repro_h1_01.sh (kinetics, the head's own service on bh_h1_r1); bughunt/notes/H1/scripts/concurrent_same.py ORIGIN PROJECT DB VALUE 4 for the mirror engine
candidates.expected: One row whose body by and created_by both name the first asker, and every asker answered with that asker's name.
candidates.observed: kinetics: run 7bae0ae9211431bf created_by asker-2, body by asker-0; 6cfdda5438758bf7 created_by asker-0, by asker-3; 5ee04828025b6941 created_by asker-3, by asker-2. mirror: run cd9933cb5a7834e9 answered asker-0, asker-1 and asker-2 each by its own name; the row then held created_by asker-1, body by asker-2, and GET /api/runs served asker-2.
candidates.cause: core/openferment_core/engine/runs.py:463-467 and 484 (keep_run reads the held row, then writes with rows.put, an upsert that keeps the first created_by and replaces the body: core/openferment_core/db/rows.py:61-66); the check-then-compute window is runs.py:867-875 (run_engine) and 546-561 (compute_kept), with no lock or insert-once write
candidates.evidence: Four threads behind a barrier POST the same body with by asker-0..3; three kinetics values and five mirror values each gave one row whose created_by and body by differ (psql on openferment.runs).

candidates.title: An engine set aside for its name or a failed import leaves cobra in the service process
candidates.statement: An entry module that imports a worker library and is then set aside for another reason (an object misnamed, an import that raises) leaves that library in the service's process, its words never name it, and a later engine whose entry module imports the same library loads with no word said.
candidates.contract: CLAUDE.md:41: "BioSTEAM, thermosteam, biorefineries, the vendored SFF toolkit and cobra run in worker processes ...; the service process imports none of them"; docs/api/engines.md:141-144: "An entry module whose import brings into the service's process ... one of `biosteam`, `thermosteam`, `biorefineries`, `pisces_sff` and `cobra` is set aside, those modules named."
candidates.reproCommand: bughunt/notes/H1/scripts/repro_probe.sh (H1-02 section: bughunt/notes/H1/scripts/heavy_left.py over the stand-in package bughunt/notes/H1/scripts/probe-engine)
candidates.expected: cobra out of the service's process after discovery; h1z-heavy-unseen, whose entry module imports cobra, set aside with cobra named, as it is when it loads alone.
candidates.observed: h1z-heavy-unseen alone: set aside, cobra named, cobra out after discovery. With h1a-misnamed-heavy (set aside for its name) or h1b-fails-heavy (ImportError after importing cobra) loaded first: h1z-heavy-unseen LOADED with no error, and cobra in sys.modules after discovery; the running service listed h1z-heavy-unseen with 18 things and its worker ready.
candidates.cause: core/openferment_core/engine/registry.py:246-267: the modules an import added are counted and taken out of sys.modules only when _why_not passes (255-260); the failed-load return at 251-252 and a _why_not refusal both leave them, so the next entry point's `before` already holds cobra
candidates.evidence: heavy_left.py narrows registry.entry_points to the names given, imports openferment_core.api as the service does, and prints each h1 engine's verdict and whether cobra stands in sys.modules.

candidates.title: The documented conform command for a scenario flowsheet fails with ProjectRequired
candidates.statement: `python -m openferment_core.engine.conform biosteam --thing ethanol_glucose_v0 --inputs <file>` stops with `ProjectRequired: This names no project` and keeps no verdict, with the values set or without them; the same command with OPENFERMENT_PROJECT set to any id makes the eight checks.
candidates.contract: docs/api/engines.md:670-672: "`python -m openferment_core.engine.conform biosteam --thing ethanol_glucose_v0 --inputs <file>`. Named with a value it waits for left unset, the thing cannot run as it stands (the engine's `unready`), and the command refuses it in words"; docs/BASE.md:44: "`biosteam --thing <a scenario flowsheet> --inputs <file>`, the values a scenario flowsheet waits for"
candidates.expected: The eight checks made on ethanol_glucose_v0 with the file's values; with no file, the refusal naming the six values that wait.
candidates.observed: "✗ the checks could not be made on biosteam: openferment_core.projects.ProjectRequired: This names no project. ...", exit 1, both with the six values set and with none; with OPENFERMENT_PROJECT=any-id the checks ran and the no-file case gave the documented words.
candidates.cause: core/openferment_core/engine/conform.py:1046-1053: _inside asks the engine's unready (BiosteamEngine.unready, engine/biosteam.py:284-305, which reads the Proforma provider's parameters and needs a current project) before the checks' project is made and entered at 1054-1055
candidates.evidence: Ran the command from the head's venv on a fresh bh_h1_r3 with a six-value inputs file; then again with OPENFERMENT_PROJECT set.

candidates.cause: core/openferment_core/workers/proforma_worker.py:180-202 keeps one built system per flowsheet (_BUILT) and evaluates every case on it in turn; core/openferment_core/flowsheets/ethanol_glucose_v0.py:199-230 empties the recycles and resets the TEA's secant, and the first simulate of a fresh build still lands in another state (stream 12's pressure among the differences).
